Re: Customer Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Member: Rowan Grant  
Member ID: W574273539  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA — Colorado  
Requested service: Total shoulder replacement  
CPT: 23472  
Reference number: POC-B9867C3E93-20631  
Date of denial notice: August 4, 2026

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Cigna’s denial of prior authorization for total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472. I request that Cigna overturn the denial and authorize the procedure based on the documented clinical findings summarized below.

The publicly available Cigna/EviCore policy identified for this procedure is CMM-318, CIGNA Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal CMM-318: Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Resurfacing/Revision/Arthrodesis, effective March 7, 2026. The policy states:

“Total shoulder arthroplasty (replacement) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:”

“Function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment) for at least three (3) months.”

“Failure of at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management.”

“Radiographic imaging and/or an advanced diagnostic procedure (i.e., MRI, CT scan), which is conclusive for the presence of advanced destructive degenerative joint disease (i.e., osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis) that correlates with the individual’s reported symptoms and physical exam findings including marked narrowing of the joint space and ONE OR MORE of the following:”

“Irregular joint surfaces”

“Glenoid sclerosis”

“Glenoid osteophyte changes”

“Flattened glenoid”

“Cystic changes in the humeral head”

The available records address these requirements as follows:

1. Function-limiting pain for more than three months

The shoulder pain has progressively worsened for nine months despite rest. The condition substantially limits daily functioning: I cannot reach overhead, dress without assistance, or sleep on the affected side. Examination documents glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees.

2. Failure of non-surgical treatment

The records document prolonged provider-directed conservative treatment, including:

- NSAID treatment for four months, with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on March 23, 2026, which provided only three weeks of partial relief; and
- Sixteen supervised physical-therapy visits from April 12, 2026, through June 21, 2026, focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening.

Despite these measures, the pain and functional limitations have continued to progress. The physical-therapy discharge note documents completion of the supervised therapy course.

3. Imaging-confirmed advanced degenerative joint disease

Shoulder radiographs obtained on May 21, 2026, using true AP and axillary views, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT imaging confirms an intact rotator cuff. These findings correlate with the reported pain, restricted motion, crepitus, and loss of function.

The imaging therefore documents severe structural joint disease, including marked joint-space loss, glenoid sclerosis, osteophyte formation, and a flattened glenoid. The intact rotator cuff also supports the requested anatomic total shoulder replacement rather than indicating that the requested procedure is clinically inappropriate.

4. No documented contraindication

The records do not show active infection, untreated substance use, or other documented contraindication to surgery. The BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker. Cuff strength is intact.

Based on the nine-month symptom history, failure of medication, injection, and supervised physical therapy, severe functional impairment, and imaging-confirmed destructive glenohumeral disease, the requested procedure meets the medical-necessity requirements identified above.

Please conduct a full appeal review by a reviewer who was not involved in the initial denial. Please overturn the denial and authorize CPT 23472. If Cigna continues to deny the request, please provide the specific criterion that Cigna believes has not been met, identify the clinical information relied upon, and provide the applicable next-level or external-review instructions.

Enclosed are the supporting records, including the physical-therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, May 21, 2026 radiographs, CT findings, examination findings, and the original denial notice.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal.

Sincerely,

Rowan Grant
